# Bridge to the research code {#sec-bridge}

## Question

Every toy in this book has a production counterpart in `revisit_sobolev`.
Where exactly, and what does the production version add? This is the only
chapter that imports the research code.

## The map

| educational object | chapter | production equivalent |

## What the production versions add

Real atoms: thousands of levels and up to a million lines per ion, with
Saha–Boltzmann populations and stimulated emission in the depths. Exact
Doppler factors and a clock carried by each packet, so that the expansion
work is booked, not ignored. Multi-shell states with a density and
temperature structure from published models, transported as a union of the
shells' line sets. Two coarse-grained opacities, expansion and line-binned,
whose closures against the resolved transport are Paper IV's subject. And
the discipline that this book borrows: every number in a manuscript
generated from a frozen record; every reading pre-declared with a gray
outcome; a claim read through with the numbers substituted before
submission.

## The same numbers, side by side

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
import sys, pathlib
root = pathlib.Path("../..").resolve()
sys.path.insert(0, str(root)); sys.path.insert(0, str(root / "paper2/phase1")); sys.path.insert(0, str(pathlib.Path("../src").resolve()))
import numpy as np
from sobolev.optical_depth import tau_sobolev                 # the production formula
from rtedu.sobolev import tau_sobolev_toy, toy_line_list      # the toy
L = toy_line_list()
tau_prod = tau_sobolev(L["f_osc"], L["n_l"], 2.99792458e10 / L["nu_lines"], L["t"])
print("toy      :", np.round(L["tau"][:4], 4))
print("production:", np.round(tau_prod[:4], 4))
print("identical to", float(np.max(np.abs(tau_prod - L["tau"]) / L["tau"])), "relative")
```

```{python}
#| echo: true
#| code-fold: false
from sobolev.macroatom import DownwardMacroAtom               # the production macroatom
from rtedu.atom import five_level_atom
from rtedu.macroatom import ToyMacroAtom
a = five_level_atom()
prod = DownwardMacroAtom(a.nu, a.A, a.lower, a.upper, np.ones(a.n_lines), a.E)
toy = ToyMacroAtom(a)
k, p_de, p_jp = toy.probabilities(4)
ul, pd_, pi_ = prod.probabilities(4)
print("toy de-activation  :", np.round(p_de, 4))
print("production         :", np.round(pd_, 4))
print("toy jump           :", np.round(p_jp, 4))
print("production         :", np.round(pi_, 4))
```

The two macroatoms are given the same five-level atom and the same escape
probabilities; the production one is the class the Paper IV fluorescence
legs use. If the four rows above agree, the toy of chapter 8 and the
research code share their physics to the last digit, and the difference
between this book and Paper IV is only the atom.

## What would fail if our assumption were wrong?

If the production macroatom used different weights, or booked energy
differently from chapter 7, the numbers above would not agree and the
reader could not trust that the toy taught the right thing. That is why
this chapter runs, rather than describes, the comparison.
